title: LoopGuardPolicy
description: Limits for one root run of an agent loop (F-REL-09). A run is every provider call that shares a root run id (see README 'Loop guard'). Before each provider call the guard compares the run's state with these limits; every limit is optional, and a null limit is never breached. A limit is the amount the run may consume: a breach is evaluated before a call and happens once the limit is reached, so `maxSteps: 25` allows 25 calls and refuses the 26th, and `maxCostUsd: 1.0` refuses the first call that starts at or above $1.00 of recorded spend.

maxSteps.description: Maximum provider calls in one run. A call that was refused by the guard is not a step.

maxCostUsd.description: Maximum recorded spend of one run in USD. Cost is only known after a call, so the guard compares the spend of the calls already made, not an estimate of the next one.

maxWallTimeSeconds.description: Maximum seconds from the run's first provider call to the start of the next one.

maxRepeatedToolCalls.description: Stop a run that keeps asking for the same tool call: breached once any one (tool name, arguments hash) has been requested this many times in the run. The arguments hash is ToolCall.arguments_hash (F-ADP-03), so key order and whitespace do not matter and the arguments themselves are never stored.

action.description: What happens on a breach. stop refuses the call; fallback lets it through on `fallbackModel`; dry_run only records the breach and lets the call through unchanged.

fallbackModel.description: Required when action is fallback, ignored otherwise.
